observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a wall-length mirror on the left, sage-green curtains, light wood flooring, and on the right a potted plant, two lighting stands and a floor fan. A barefoot woman in a pink short-sleeved top and grey flared trousers stands with her back to a static camera, holding an open paper parasol overhead in her right hand; her reflection in the mirror shows her front (the mirror image is the same person, not a second dancer).
visible_changes: The camera and background objects (mirror frame, curtains, stands, fan, plant) stay fixed in pixel position throughout, so all apparent motion is the dancer's own body, not camera movement.
The dancer's lower body shifts from a near-upright stance (frames 1-6) into a bent-knee plié with the hips lowering (frames 7-16), while the left heel rises off the floor.

The left leg then lifts into the air with a pointed toe (roughly frames 17-24), returns toward the floor (frames 25-30), and ends with the left foot placed behind/on the toe near the right leg (frames 31-41).
The left arm leaves the hip (around frame 17), sweeps down and back, then extends outward to the side at shoulder/waist height with the hand pointing, and finally draws back in (frames 34-41).
The parasol remains held overhead but its canopy tilts and rotates relative to the head over the clip, ending at a more slanted angle.
The torso and head rotate slightly, and these changes are reproduced in the mirror reflection.
The right foot stays planted as the support foot for the whole excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The full choreography before t=0 and after t=2.67s is not shown; the clip begins and ends mid-movement.
Whether the dancer travels across the floor beyond these small in-place adjustments is not visible.
Any accompanying music or intent of the routine is unseen.
uncertain_details: Exact dance terminology for the footwork (plié, tendu, etc.) is not confirmed by the frames.
Precise moments when the left foot fully leaves versus touches the floor are hard to pin down frame-by-frame.
Minor differences in limb angles between the real view and the mirror view are due to perspective, not a separate motion.
